full_description: Amarylis is looking for one of its clients a. Industrial Director. Are you looking for a new professional experience in the pharmaceutical industry on an industrial site? Here is the ideal opportunity for you to invest yourself in a strategic role with high impact. Apply now! As the true pilot of the site, you will be responsible for ensuring its overall performance and sustainable development. In this capacity, you will be responsible for:

01/02/2026  
The position is part of the ANR MilaDy project - Machine Learning Modeling for Turbulent Dynamos (2026-2030), coordinated by C. Nore (LISN, University of Paris-Saclay), S. Cheng (CEREA, ENPC), with Y. Ponty (Observatory of the Côte d'Azur) and F. Marcotte (INRIA Côte d'Azur).  
The project aims to elucidate the mechanisms of self-generation and inversion of magnetic fields in moving conductive fluids, phenomena characteristic of planetary cores and stellar interiors. To do so, it combines high-performance numerical simulation (HPC) and machine learning to design reduced predictive models capable of reproducing the complex dynamics of turbulent magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows.  
The postdoctoral researcher will participate in modeling, analyzing, and interpreting large databases from 3D MHD simulations. They will develop and apply advanced methods for dimensionality reduction, rare event detection, and multiple attractor characterization, relying on modern machine learning and latent representation approaches (autoencoders, physics-informed models, contrastive learning). Particular attention will be paid to linking the learned structures with physical invariants and flow control parameters.  
The postdoctoral researcher will be hosted at the Lagrange laboratory (OCA, Nice), closely connected with the Castor team (INRIA Côte d'Azur), and will actively collaborate with the entire MilaDy consortium (LISN, CEREA).  
Main activities:  
- Generate data from DNS/LES simulations of turbulent MHD flows representative of planetary and experimental dynamos (e.g., DRESDYN).  
- Manage and structure large multidimensional datasets from these simulations.  
- Develop and train models for dimensional reduction, dynamical regime prediction, and rare event detection.  
- Design and train compression and latent representation models respecting physical constraints (physics-aware encoders/decoders);  
- Analyze and interpret latent spaces to relate learned representations to physical flow parameters;  
- Evaluate learning models using physical coherence metrics (energy spectra, helicity, divergence, magnetic topology);  
- Integrate physical constraints into learning architectures.  
- Disseminate results via publications, presentations, and ANR deliverables.  
Required knowledge:  
- Parallel numerical simulation (DNS, LES, MPI/OpenMP codes).  
- Data and model reduction.  
- Machine learning applied to numerical physics: convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, attention-based networks, contrastive learning, or physics-informed models (PINNs).  
- Handling and preprocessing large data volumes (HDF5, NetCDF, PyTorch DataLoader, etc.).  
- Scientific computing tools: Python (NumPy, PyTorch, TensorFlow), C++ for simulation parts.  
- Statistical analysis and scientific data visualization.  
- Good knowledge of Linux and high-performance computing environments.  
Recruitment level and required degrees  
- PhD completed  
Salary  
Based on the public service pay scale for researcher bodies, variable depending on experience. The gross annual salary corresponds to experience level.  
To apply  
Please send your CV and cover letter simultaneously by email to the manager Yannick.Ponty@oca.eu, copying Human Resources at recrutement@oca.eu. All our positions are open to persons with disabilities.

job_title: Post-doctorate Aggregation and fragmentation of flexible fibers (M/F)
full_description: We are looking for our future Postdoctoral Researcher! The turbulent dynamics of macroscopic fibers involve complex interaction between translation and deformation at multiple spatial and temporal scales. Its study represents a major challenge compared to microscopic objects, whose deformation is mainly influenced by velocity gradients. The understanding of macroscopic fiber behavior in turbulence remains largely unexplored despite its critical implications for natural systems (plankton colonies), industrial processes (paper manufacturing), and environmental concerns (plastic debris in oceans). Previous research on fiber dynamics in turbulence has mainly focused on isolated objects and examined tumbling and rotation motions, statistical properties of deformation, and interactions with coherent structures. Despite these efforts, fundamental questions regarding the dynamics of individual fibers remain unresolved, and there is a significant gap in our understanding of collective behavior of fiber ensembles. This postdoc is part of a larger project aiming to understand and model fiber fragmentation and aggregation processes. The project relies on a multidisciplinary approach, combining mathematical modeling, numerical simulations, statistical physics, and laboratory experiments. Join us at Université Côte d'Azur, recognized since 2016 for its scientific and educational excellence, to build together the model of the 21st-century responsible and innovative university. Your missions The objective is to develop coarse-grained mesoscopic models for long, thin, flexible fibers such as slender bodies or articulated chains, to accurately account for breakages, knots, fiber-fiber interactions, and entanglement. These models will be used to understand how these processes are influenced by turbulent fluctuations, aiming to provide a full statistical representation in idealized flows, with and without boundaries. This will support the development of macroscopic descriptions necessary to address long-term global evolutions in realistic contexts. Proposed methodology: The proposed method consists of using simplified coarse-grained fiber models, such as slender body theory and bead-spring chains used in the kinetic theory of polymer solutions. These models will be implemented in existing highly parallel spectral codes, capable of accurately resolving the full complexity of turbulent flows. Simulations will be performed in idealized geometries, including homogeneous isotropic turbulence, channel flows, and Couette flows. Medium-sized simulations will use the HPC cluster "Azzurra" of Université Côte d'Azur, while the largest and most computationally demanding simulations will be conducted in national computing centers. This position is for you if You have significant programming experience (preferably in C or C++), a good command of English. job_title: Postdoctoral researcher in aquatic microbial ecology (M/F)
full_description: Complete profile on the UCA website: 2025095A The response of microbial communities to disturbances is determined by two key properties: resistance, that is, the capacity of a community to remain unchanged in the face of a disturbance, and resilience, that is, the speed at which a community returns to its pre-disturbance state. The characteristics of individual members as well as the overall diversity of the community can influence the resistance and resilience of bacterioplankton communities, thus affecting their dynamics in fluctuating environments. Although a high proportion of resistant or resilient members is associated with greater community-level stability, the role of diversity in promoting resistance and resilience is often attributed to functional redundancy between species, a phenomenon known as the "insurance effect." According to this effect, functional losses caused by sensitive species during environmental disturbances can be compensated by less sensitive and functionally redundant taxa, allowing the maintenance of the overall community function. Preliminary results suggest that the relative importance of diversity structures compared to species-specific properties for determining community-level responses to disturbances depends on the eutrophication level of aquatic environments. This could be explained by the fact that the expression of resistance seems related to metabolic costs, themselves constrained by nutrient availability. RESPONSIBILITIES AND OBJECTIVES OF THE POSITION: The selected candidate will join the LMGE MEB team within the GENMOD project, under the supervision of Dr. Sara BEIER. He/she will analyze metatranscriptome datasets from aquatic environments with varying levels of eutrophication, to assess how the community-wide transcriptional activities respond to environmental fluctuations. Specifically, the research will aim to determine whether transcriptional stability results from: - Community members having high tolerance and, consequently, high transcriptional stability in response to environmental fluctuations, or - The insurance effect, through alternating transcriptional activities of functionally redundant taxa within the community, which compensate for transcriptional changes of individual community members. The project will involve both the use of already existing metatranscriptome datasets and contribution to the generation of new datasets. The candidate will mainly focus on the analysis of metatranscriptome data but will also participate in laboratory and/or field work necessary for dataset creation. full_description: Context The Scientific Computing Service of ILL currently offers a postdoctoral researcher position. The selected candidate will be responsible for developing a software solution for a strategy of neutron diffraction data reduction and acquisition on protein single crystals. These data are collected using one of the two quasi-Laue diffractometers LADI or DALI. Data can be obtained between 1.5 and 2.5 Å to locate protons or deuterons of special interest, water structures or other small molecules which can be deuterium-labeled to make them particularly visible. Data collection is possible for samples whose unit cell dimensions range between 50 and ~150 Å and crystal volumes from ~0.05 to 0.5 mm³. Your duties As a member of the Scientific Computing Service, you will work closely with other services within the ILL Science Division and notably with the Large Scale Structures group and scientists responsible for LADI and DALI diffractometers. The currently used software for data reduction is LAUEGEN, an obsolete and unsupported software. We plan to extend the features of our in-house software ESMERALDA (used for data reduction from Laue diffraction patterns on single crystals in condensed matter studies) to process the large unit cells characteristic of biological samples. ESMERALDA is an application written in Fortran 2008 that uses many crystallographic routines embedded in the CrysFML08 library (https://code.ill.fr). You will perform the following tasks: - Establish data reduction/analysis workflows adapted to quasi-Laue methods to meet scientists' needs; - Develop code and, optionally, a specific graphical user interface (GUI); - Validate software solutions; - Write documentation; - Participate in scientific experiments on LADI/DALI. You will work in an international multidisciplinary environment, interact with scientists, and be encouraged to pursue or initiate your own scientific activities. However, your main activity will consist in validating and providing a robust and professional software solution for processing LADI/DALI data. Your profile - You hold a PhD in physics, chemistry, or life sciences and have a particular interest in diffraction experiments and structure determination. - Alternatively, you hold a master’s degree in computer science and proven experience in a scientific environment or scientific software development. - You have solid experience in Python, Fortran, or C++ and good software development practices (e.g., version control with Git). - Knowledge of crystallography would be an asset. - Good knowledge of English is required; knowledge of French or willingness to learn it is desired (training provided by ILL). You can apply online via our application portal, including a publication list and names of 3 references, including one from your current workplace, quoting reference number 25/15. Applications are accepted until a candidate meeting the requirements is selected.

full_description:
Context: Collaborative project between the LOCIE, LGCgE laboratories and ATLANTIC and DATE companies within the framework of the ANR PRCE "MOTUS" project (Bio-based latent storage integrated into a heat pump for optimizing energy performance, noise reduction, and flexibility).  
The postdoctoral researcher will be based at LGCgE in Béthune and will be involved in the ANR project.  

ANR project summary:  
Decarbonization is a major climate challenge that involves heavy use of heat pumps (HP) in the building sector, as well as the use of low-GWP refrigerants.  
The development of HPs is constrained by size, aesthetics, and acoustics, particularly for outdoor air HPs which are the most widespread (lower cost).  
This project proposes to integrate a storage with phase change materials (bio-based PCM) into the evaporator of an indoor propane heat pump in order, on the one hand, to improve flexibility and energy performance as has been widely studied, and on the other hand to reduce the outdoor air flow rate (allowing air draw-off outside HP operating periods) which currently leads to strong noise disturbances.  
The objective is a halving of the air flow rate resulting in a 10 dB(A) reduction in acoustic power. This point is the reason for the MOTUS project, which has never been considered in the numerous scientific publications combining HP and PCM.  
Given the narrow operating temperature ranges of HP, a storage with PCM will be considered.  
The MOTUS project aims to improve the characterization of bio-based PCMs thanks to a flow bench, notably in the case of PCM with supercooling subjected to partial melting-solidification cycles corresponding to more realistic operating modes.  
The modeling and optimization of the hybrid evaporator will aim to limit calculation times related to annual dynamic simulations.  
We will optimize with a multicriteria approach an air-water HP, supplying heating (space heating and DHW) and cooling needs.  
Decision parameters will correspond to the sizing of the air heater and the hybrid evaporator.  
Performance functions will notably include air flow reduction (noise nuisance), cost, SCOP, and size.  

Postdoc mission summary:  
The postdoctoral researcher will work on the state of the art of bio-based PCMs and their characterization (Task 2/TRL1) with a flow bench (large volume: approximately 270 cm3).  
LGCgE will subcontract DSC measurements on a few mg of PCM.  
Three characterization approaches can thus be compared with very different sample sizes.  
The postdoctoral researcher will also work on the characterization of the initial version of the hybrid evaporator (EH-V0).

Main missions:

. Conduct technical and regulatory monitoring on renewable energies

The project focuses on two pilot species and zones: spruce around Grand Est, affected by drought and bark beetles, and oak around Centre-Val de Loire, facing a growing dieback phenomenon linked to drought and heat waves. You will work within the P2E (Physiology, Ecology and Environment) laboratory at the University of Orléans.  
The Trees and Responses to Water and Environmental Constraints Research Team is a multidisciplinary group bringing together researchers in ecology, remote sensing, ecophysiology, physiology, microbiology, and molecular biology.  
The general research theme of the ARCHE team is the study of ecological, physiological, and molecular determinants involved in acclimation, resilience, and adaptation of plants in a global change context.  
The group includes three thematic axes (Ecophysiology, Epigenetics, and Phytomanagement), thus addressing questions at different scales.  
Mission  
As a research engineer in the project, you will be in charge of:  
1) Producing and analyzing dieback maps over the past 5 years using Sentinel-2 time series and the RECONFORT and FORDEAD tools.

Field validation campaigns are also planned throughout the project.  
Regular meetings will be organized to monitor work progress, particularly with the SME TERRANIS based in Toulouse, specialized in the design, development, and marketing of geoinformation services derived from satellite imagery.

DESIRED PROFILE

Mission:  
Within the framework of the Climate Change Initiative (CCI) River Discharge project of the European Space Agency (ESA), the proposed mission consists of improving the calculation of long-term time series (over 20 years or more) of river water levels measured by several radar altimetry satellite missions, as well as estimating their uncertainty.  
This work will be done using already processed water level series, with the use of Level 2 satellite altimetry products and reprocessed data by LEGOS/CTOH (Center for Topography of Oceans and Hydrosphere).  
Existing processing chains developed to obtain long water level and discharge time series will have to be used and improved, but especially to determine and analyze the impact of certain sources of error on the water levels.  
The contribution of the new SWOT wide-swath altimetry mission ( https://swot.jpl.nasa.gov /) will also be investigated.  
The water level series and associated documentation will have to be delivered, first internally within the project (in France, Italy, and Germany), then officially to the European Space Agency (ESA) for certain deadlines set in agreement with ESA.  
The position will be based at the Laboratory of Geophysical and Spatial Oceanography Studies (LEGOS), under the direct supervision of Sylvain BIANCAMARIA (LEGOS), in close collaboration with Fernando NIÑO (LEGOS), Fabien BLAREL (LEGOS), and Fabrice PAPA (LEGOS).  
The work will be done in collaboration with companies HydroMatters, Eola, and CLS.  
Activities:  
Radar nadir altimetry is currently used by the scientific community to observe the dynamics of water levels in rivers under the satellite track. These data have been used since the 1990s and a long archive of measurements is now available, allowing the prospect of estimating the temporal dynamics of rivers at the climate scale and at various places in watersheds.  
When discharge data are available, the calculation of the rating curve between discharge and altimetric water level allows converting satellite water levels into discharge.  
Based on this proven methodology, the pioneering CCI River Discharge project ( https://climate.esa.int/fr/projets/river-discharge /) is developing a river discharge product (currently at 53 sites).  
This project underwent an initial phase between 2023 and 2024 and has been extended for a second development phase until the end of December 2026.  
The proposed position is part of this project, specifically on the calculation of water levels by satellite altimetry.  
The aim of the work is to improve the altimetry water level time series and the estimation of some error sources in these series, which will be used to derive the altimetry discharge product.  
About 3 months of the contract time will be dedicated to improving the water level time series to better characterize the bias between these series depending on the satellite mission.  
The impact of taking river slope into account will also be investigated on the calculation of water levels for each mission to compensate for the + or – 1 km drift of the satellites' ground track.  
The contribution of the new wide-swath altimetry mission SWOT (launched in December 2022) for these long series will also be studied.  
About 7 months of the contract time will be dedicated to estimating the water levels of various altimetry missions using a new data processing algorithm called SpecR.  
The task is not to develop the algorithm but to use it by automating the processing chain, ensuring run and parameter traceability, setting up a quality approach, then running SpecR on the 53 identified sites for the Jason-1/2/3, Sentinel-3A/B, and Sentinel-6 satellite altimetry missions (Envisat will be considered if SpecR can be adapted for this mission).  
Between 200 and 300 time series will have to be generated with SpecR.  
The water level time series obtained with SpecR will then be compared with those obtained in the first phase of the project, which used a classical altimetry data processing algorithm, as well as with in situ data where available.  
This work will estimate the sensitivity of water levels to altimetry data processing algorithms.

job_title: Thesis: Thin-film TTS for aero tribological application (M/F)
full_description:
In line with the functional needs of Safran Group's future products, the Materials & Processes division identifies, proposes, and develops innovative solutions. Within the Materials and Processes division, the coatings service, in which this thesis is situated, develops technical solutions to protect materials and improve their properties.  
Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used for their exceptional non-stick, hydrophobic and chemical properties. However, their environmental persistence and toxic effects on human health have led to strict regulations and active research for substitutes.  
Various ceramic coatings produced by PVD processes such as DLC (Diamond-like carbon) or BAM + TiB2 (Magnesium Aluminum Boride) appear as promising alternatives due to their chemical resistance, low friction, and biocompatibility.  
This thesis aims to explore the feasibility of replacing PFAS with BAM + TiB2 coatings in various aeronautical applications.  
In the aeronautics sector, PFAS are commonly used in the following applications:  
- Anti-icing coatings on wings and sensors  
- Protection of electrical and electronic components against humidity and corrosion  
- Non-stick and lubricating coatings in mechanical systems subjected to extreme stresses (pivot joints, sliding joints, to promote sliding between two parts, to reduce friction coefficient)  
- Hydrophobic and oleophobic treatments for composite materials and interior textiles  
BAM + TiB2 coatings offer an interesting alternative due to:  
- Their low friction coefficient and wear resistance  
- Their thermal and chemical resistance  
- Their adjustable hydrophobicity for anti-icing surfaces  
- Their compatibility with metal and composite substrates, widely used in aeronautics  
One of the challenges will be to optimize the process and characteristics of BAM + TiB2 deposits to achieve performance levels equivalent to PFAS in terms of friction coefficient and resistance (inertia) to aeronautical fluids.  
The study will combine experimental and theoretical approaches to:  
1. Synthesize and characterize different types of BAM + TiB2 coatings to optimize their anti-adhesive and hydrophobic properties  
2. Evaluate their performance under real conditions compared to PFAS-based coatings (wear resistance, chemical inertia, thermal stability)  
3. Analyze their environmental and toxicological impact to ensure safety and regulatory compliance  
4. Explore the physico-chemical mechanisms explaining the adhesion and wettability of BAM + TiB2 surfaces, with a view to improving their formulation.  
Job location: Limoges (IRCER, SAFIR platform)  
Travel in France to academic sites and Group companies for characterizations  
Supervision will be carried out by Safran, IRCER and LTDS.

We continually look for technological advances. This commitment to innovation extends beyond new products and processes to encompass how we can positively impact the life of people all over the world. Sustainability, climate change, digitalization, holistic-multi material approach to construction are the pillars of our today activities. To address the urgent societal need for science-based management recommendations for forests under increasing pressure, and to leverage the fast-developing expertise in multi-disciplinary forest research in Luxembourg, LIST, in collaboration with the University of Luxembourg and the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research, has formed a dedicated doctoral training unit (DTU) on "Forest function under stress" (FORFUS). It consists of 4 inter-linked research clusters, focusing on below-ground processes, tree and canopy processes, remote sensing observations, and prediction and valuation of forest functions, providing a holistic view on forests as complex systems. See the project website to find out more about the FORFUS doctoral training unit: https://www.list.lu/en/research/project/forfus Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu / How will you contribute? Forest resilience is defined as the ability of the ecosystem to recover from perturbations that eventually lead the system to a different state. In such definition, vulnerability quantifies the degree of the forest ecosystem response to such external perturbations. Climate and human-induced disturbances may alter forest ecosystems dynamics, modifying eventually their resilience to rapidly changing conditions. Previous studies based on the temporal analysis of remote sensing indices suggest a change in the resilience of forest ecosystems, with a declining trend for temperate forests. However, it is still unclear how such changing resilience emerge from altered short-term physiological responses of tree species and modified long-term dynamics of the whole ecosystem. On the other hand, vegetation demography models are numerical tools formulating forest processes based on a classification of similarly sized individuals (i.e., cohorts) within the same class of biomes. Such an approach is suitable for capturing nonlinear size- and trait-dependent ecosystem responses to droughts and heatwaves, which in turn feedback to the distribution of species, modulating the long-term ecosystem resilience to environmental changes. In this framework, the objectives of your research activities are: O1: Explain ecosystem response to drought and heatwave events based on diversity in plant hydraulic traits and competition amongst different plant water use strategies. O2: Assess how alternative CO2 concentration trajectories will result in altered ecosystem dynamics and resilience. O3: Evaluate the ecosystem resilience simulated by a vegetation demography model with emerging signals extracted from multi-spectral remote sensing products and dendrochronology data This position is part of the doctoral training unit FORFUS ( https://www.list.lu/en/research/project/forfus ), associated with the FORLUX ( https://www.list.lu/en/research/project/forlux ) research project, both of which together will include 13 doctoral candidates and 4 postdoctoral researchers. full_description: 4. Temporary contract | Up to 48 months (14 months initial contract) | Belval Are you passionate about research? So are we! You will be part of the LIST Materials Research and Technology department, where you will carry out your work in the Quantum Materials Group, led by Dr. Florian Kaiser. Within our ERC Consolidator Project “Q-Chip”, you will define the new standard in the scalability of solid-state quantum systems. How? You benefit from the vast potential of our industry-compatible semiconductor quantum platform, i.e., colour centres in silicon carbide. You will integrate multiple electrical and optical control structures on a quantum chip, which unlocks completely new ways of operating quantum systems. Your PhD thesis objectives include: (a) Strongly increasing the quantum algorithm depth that we can implement with nuclear spin qubits in silicon carbide. You will bring to live a novel concept that we have developed, which reduces two-qubit gate durations by at least one order of magnitude. This technique is unique to silicon carbide qubits and requires implementing high-speed magnetic field tuning lines at a nanoscale. (b) Demonstrating the first scalable electro-optic quantum chip in silicon carbide based on parallelised nanoscale electric field tuning. You will design and farbicate a quantum chip that incorporates Stark shift electrodes around several colour centres. This will allow you to make them operate at the same wavelength, a fundamental prerequisite for creating entanglement amongst them via photonic interference. Additionally, you will demonstrate high-speed electro-optic switches on our silicon-carbide-strontium-titanate hybrid platform, which unlocks the ultimate scalability potential of the platform. (c) The final goal is to combine the above techniques to create the first functional silicon carbide quantum chip, and to demonstrate its operation, e.g., creation of photon-mediated entanglement between distant nuclear spin qubits. The ESG & Decarbonization Program Lead Specialist will lead the implementation of Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), decarbonization strategies, and ESG compliance across the Rails business unit. full_description: 1. SD-25102 POST-DOCTORAL POSITION IN ENVIRONMENTAL GEOCHEMISTRY 24 months contract | Belvaux-Luxembourg Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a Research and Technology Organization (RTO) active in the fields of materials, environment and IT. By transforming scientific knowledge into technologies, smart data and tools, LIST empowers citizens in their choices, public authorities in their decisions and businesses in their strategies. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu / Finding new innovative ways of managing water resources, while preserving freshwater ecosystems and ensuring equitable access to their services, is a major challenge that must be addressed by accounting for the intertwining of societies and ecosystems. To advance research on this burning topic, the WATERWEAVE project, funded through the Water4All call between European Union and French, Brazilian and Luxembourgish funding agencies, brings together an interdisciplinary and international consortium to develop an integrative and interactive tool (IIT) to promote social learning and help managing water resources and freshwater ecosystems in a context of land-use and climatic change. The IIT will represent ecosystem functioning and ecosystem service provision and multi-agent-based interactive models to represent the social components of the system. It will be kept simple to ensure easy handling, straightforward interpretation, and adaptability to local context. Its development will be nurtured by interactions with a panel composed by environmental managers, decision-makers, and different groups of end-users such as local traditional communities' representatives, recruited from three test sites in Brazil (São Paulo, Rio Grande do Sul and Pará states) and one in Luxembourg. How will you contribute? Within WATERWEAVE, LIST and the University of Brasilia have in charge the retrospective analysis of the selected sites by assessing the status of their river ecosystems using historical and actual biogeochemical information. During the last decade, innovations in geochemistry and analytical techniques (MC-ICP-MS) have been developed to better characterize the metal's dynamics in the environment. In environmental studies, trace elements (rare earth elements, Zn, Cu, Hg, Pb, Sr) and associated stable or radiogenic isotopes have been successfully applied for the discrimination of natural and anthropogenic sources, such as mining, metallurgy, industry, wastewater treatment plant and agriculture. Moreover, the coupling of these techniques provides a more integrative information about the origins (distinguishing natural and anthropogenic sources), biogeochemical processes, speciation of elements and associated risk to the ecosystems. The current analytical techniques offer enough accuracy and precision to combine on the same samples a multi tracing approach that makes it possible to describe with a larger holistic point of view the past evolution of human impact on aquatic ecosystems. This is a prerequisite to better constraint the prediction tools and model developments toward future river management decisions. Your contribution will be three-folds: On the one hand, your objective will be to explore geochemical datasets from historical river sediment and water samples that cover the last 40 to 20 years. The existing archives from river and lake sediment and soil alluvial cores allow to date and characterize past periods of human activity changes. You will first identify the existing data and harmonized the analytical information for determining the relevant tracers between the selected sites. For example, Pb and Sr isotopes are commonly used to trace the source of sediment and Zn and Hg isotopes can trace anthropogenic contamination. On the other hand, you will organize sampling campaigns to acquire and interpret data from new sediment cores and water samples that will be collected in two of the Brazilian sites. To support the retrospective analysis of the evolution of the socio-ecosystem, you will carry out dating of sediment deposition (210Pb, 14C) and assessing contaminants to trace human activities (206/207Pb, 86/87Sr, rare earth elements, heavy metals). This integrative approach will be used to quantify the provenance of key elements known to be associated to the anthropogenic activity developed in the watershed along the time. In addition, e-DNA will be analysed to provide extremely valuable quantitative information of the evolution of aquatic biodiversity in the sediment core's temporal window and in related water samples. Finally, you will explore using advanced statistical approaches (including machine learning) on these datasets and related socio-economic data provided by national institutions (IBGE in Brazil and STATEC in Luxembourg) the evolution of the river ecosystem quality through time. These results will be central to evidence links between ecosystem state and services and will allow the evaluation of their evolution through the lens of policies and management decisions. full_description: 2. The laboratory is a major player in Luxembourg's healthcare sector, serving the country's patients, doctors and hospitals. Under the supervision of the Ministry of Health and Social Security, the laboratory is a multidisciplinary public institution organized around six medical departments, two of which are designated as national diagnostic centers for human genetics and pathology respectively. The laboratory employs around 400 highly qualified staff with diverse backgrounds. The main purpose is to develop analytical activities and scientific expertise relating to the prevention, diagnosis and monitoring of human diseases; to act as a national control or reference laboratory; and to carry out forensic missions. The laboratory also collaborates with the University of Luxembourg and other biomedical research institutions, both nationally and internationally, on research and teaching activities. In particular, in the field of diagnostics, the laboratory covers the following fields of application: medical biology, microbiology, forensic medicine, environmental medicine, morphological and molecular pathology, and clinical genetics, as well as sequencing for rare diseases, oncology and pathogens. About the Service ‘Environmental Hygiene and Human Biological Monitoring': The Department Health Protection supports public health and health care for problems caused or aggravated by the environment, including indoor pollution, the working context, and consumer products. We fulfill this mission through servicing including expert advice, education and applied research. Our main stakeholders are the hospitals, the ministries and the services for occupational medicine in Luxembourg. The Department Health Protection hosts two Services: The Service “Environmental Hygiene and Human Biological Monitoring” carries out laboratory analyses – chemical and microbiological – in dust, air and surface samples (ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation). In parallel, the Service analyses the concentrations of substances or their metabolites directly in human medical samples, for example blood, urine, hair. The Service measures not only human biomarkers of exposure (ISO 15189 and ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation), but is expanding its portfolio of human biomarkers of effect relevant in the pathways of disease development and progression. The Service is also an active partner in the European Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals (PARC). PARC is funded by the European Union's « Horizon Europe » framework program for the period of 2021-2027. Within PARC, LNS is grant signatory for Luxembourg and key partner in several workpackages related to human biomonitoring and risk assessment for human exposure to chemicals from the indoor and occupational environment. It involves 200 partners from 28 European countries, including national and EU agencies as well as affiliated research organizations. The Service “Medical Expertise and Data Intelligence” hosts the medical, epidemiological and toxicological expertise in environmental and occupational health/medicine. The Service supports the National Service for Environmental Medicine at the Hospital Center Emile Mayrisch (CHEM) and is in charge of the European science-policy programs and the epidemiological surveys in the general and working population in Luxembourg that include human biological monitoring and/or environmental/occupational exposure assessment. At departmental level, a medical secretary and quality team support the services and the department head. So are we! Join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a Research and Technology Organization (RTO) active in materials, environment, and IT. The RPPM Group (Responsive Polymeric and Particulate Materials) is seeking an experienced and driven Senior Researcher to lead and contribute to high-impact research in functional polymers and nanocomposite development for additive manufacturing, emphasizing 3D/4D printing technologies and materials extrusion. The successful candidate will work at the interface of polymer chemistry, smart materials, and advanced manufacturing, guiding projects from concept to lab demonstration and industrial application. The position offers the chance to shape the future of functional materials for advanced applications such as wearable electronics, soft robotics, aerospace components, medical devices, etc. Key Responsibilities Acquire, coordinate, and lead collaborative national and international R&D projects in functional polymers and additive manufacturing. Experience in organizing and/or participating in multilateral research consortia (e.g., EU projects) is an advantage. Design and synthesize advanced polymer formulations tailored for additive manufacturing, especially 3D/4D printing and reactive extrusion. Develop and process responsive polymer-based materials and formulations for AM with tunable properties (e.g., shape-memory, stimuli-responsive). Apply and optimize 3D/4D printing techniques within broader additive manufacturing strategies, including multi-material integration and functional gradient design. Conduct thorough structural, rheological, and functional characterization to validate performance across scales. Translate lab-scale developments into functional demonstrators for targeted industrial valorization. Collaborate across disciplines on topics like (nano)-composites, smart films, membranes, high-performance, and recyclable polymers. Mentor junior researchers and foster innovation within a multidisciplinary team. Is your profile described below? Are you our future colleague? Apply now! Education · PhD in Polymer Science, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or related field, with 5–7+ years of relevant post-PhD experience. Experience and skills Deep expertise in polymer science and engineering, focusing on functional, sustainable, and high-performance polymers and formulations. Practical experience in additive manufacturing, with mastery of 3D and 4D printing technologies. Proficiency in reactive extrusion for material development and processing. Solid knowledge of responsive materials and structure–property relationships in polymer systems. Expertise in material characterization techniques including rheology, DMA, DSC, TGA, spectroscopy, and microscopy. Proven ability to move research from lab scale to functional demonstrators and pre-industrial validation. Familiarity with applications such as wearables, soft robotics, aerospace, extra-body medical devices is a plus. Experience with multi-functional and multi-material printing including integration of mechanical, electrical, and chemical properties is an asset. Commitment to circular and sustainable material design, including recyclable and bio-based polymer systems. Strong track record in project acquisition and coordination, including proposal writing and team leadership. Excellent supervision skills with experience mentoring students and early-career researchers. Strong communication skills, written and oral, for scientific and cross-sector collaboration. Team player able to thrive in multicultural, interdisciplinary, international research environment. Language skills Strong spoken and written English mandatory. Knowledge of French, German, and/or Luxembourgish is a plus. We are seeking a researcher to work on the electrochemical synthesis of copper/carbon composite materials for a two-year position. This project is part of a large collaboration between LIST and Circuit-Foil, a copper foil manufacturing company based in Luxembourg. The candidate will focus on fabricating copper/carbon composites for various applications, including lithium-ion batteries. LIST has developed a water-based process that uses functionalized carbon materials to fabricate copper/carbon composites. The candidate will assist (explore at lab scale but also work on industrial upscaling) with the production of the materials, enhancement of the existing fabrication process, and diversification. He/she should be able to conduct measurements to explore the mechanical, electrical, and/or thermal properties of the fabricated materials, such as tensile stress and nano-indentation. The project will, for example, characterize the coefficient of thermal expansion of the composites and explore them as new copper current collectors for Li-ion batteries (with graphitic, graphitic+silicon based slurries or as Li Metal anodes). You will work in Belvaux and have regular contact with the company, with some experimentation possible at the company site. Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a Research and Technology Organization (RTO) active in the fields of materials, environment and IT. By transforming scientific knowledge into technologies, smart data and tools, LIST empowers citizens in their choices, public authorities in their decisions and businesses in their strategies. The RPPM Group (Responsive Polymeric and Particulate Materials) is seeking a Lead Research Engineer with a strong background in chemical synthesis and engineering to lead and support scale-up activities within a multidisciplinary research group focused on polymeric functional and particulate materials. The candidate will play a key role in translating lab-scale innovations into demonstrator and pilot-scale processes and will contribute to reactor setup, process optimization, and safe, efficient upscaling strategies across various research projects. This position is ideal for someone with a solid understanding of chemistry and polymer science, combined with practical experience in chemical process engineering, reactor design, and industrial transfer of materials and formulations. Key Responsibilities Lead process scale-up from lab-scale reactions to pilot and demonstrator levels, particularly for polymeric and functional materials. Perform key parameter calculations (e.g., heat/mass transfer, mixing, kinetics) to guide scale-up decisions. Design, set up, and optimize large-scale reactors and processing equipment. Collaborate with chemists and materials scientists to adapt synthetic routes for scalability and industrial relevance. Ensure safe and reproducible scale-up protocols and develop standard operating procedures. Support multiple projects within the group requiring scale-up and contribute to cross-functional teams. Interface with external partners, suppliers, and industrial collaborators to tailor scale-up strategies to meet the requirements of final applications. Lead and contribute to project acquisition and proposal development by providing strategic insights into scale-up and process feasibility across collaborative initiatives. Train and supervise junior engineers, technicians, PhD students, Postdocs, and interns in process development and safety. Is your profile described below? Are you our future colleague? Apply now! Education · PhD degree in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Applied Chemistry or a closely related field, with a strong background in chemical synthesis and materials science, with 5–7+ years of relevant experience after PhD completion. Experience and skills Demonstrated experience in chemical process scale-up, ideally including pilot plant operation and reactor design/setup. In-depth understanding of polymer chemistry, material synthesis, and process-structure relationships. Proficiency in calculating and optimizing key process parameters (e.g., residence time, mixing, energy balance). Practical experience with batch and continuous reactors, including safe handling and upscaling of reactive systems. Familiarity with polymer processing (e.g., extrusion, compounding, film casting) is a strong asset. Capability to develop scale-up strategies aligned with the performance needs of end-use applications. Ability to work across disciplines and understand both chemical and materials science challenges. Demonstrated leadership in securing competitive funding and managing research projects as Principal Investigator, with strong coordination skills and the ability to balance multiple priorities effectively. ABOUT THE LABORATOIRE NATIONAL DE SANTE The "Laboratoire national de santé" (LNS) is a public institution under the supervision of the Ministry of Health in Luxembourg. As a multidisciplinary institute, the LNS consists of four scientific departments in the fields of Medical Biology, Microbiology, Forensic Medicine, and Health Protection. In addition, the LNS also hosts the National Center of Pathology and the National Center of Genetics. The LNS has more than 400 employees from over 20 countries and has been located in Dudelange since 2013. The mission of the LNS is to develop analytical and scientific expertise related to the prevention, diagnosis, and monitoring of human diseases and to ensure the role of a national control or reference laboratory as well as to carry out forensic tasks. The institution also contributes to the development, harmonization, and promotion of technical laboratory methods in close collaboration with local and international analytical laboratories. Within the scope of its responsibilities, the LNS also leads research and teaching activities in collaboration with partners in Luxembourg and abroad. With its modern infrastructure in line with recent developments in medical and analytical sciences, the LNS is an ambitious laboratory with innovative projects that increase its expertise in public health. ABOUT THE NATIONAL CENTER OF PATHOLOGY (NCP) The National Center of Pathology has approximately 100 employees and is subdivided into two services: - The Pathological anatomy service is responsible for diagnosing cancer, precancerous, and inflammatory lesions. It includes a joint molecular pathology platform with the National Center of Genetics for identifying molecular abnormalities critical for diagnosis and treatment, particularly in cancer cases. The service comprises seven specialized units: uro/hematopathology, gastrointestinal pathology, dermato/soft tissue and head and neck pathology, gyneco-lung, non-gynecological cytology, neuropathology, and autopsy-fetal units. - The Gynecological cytology service focuses on cervical cancer screening using liquid-based cytology since 2014 and fully digital since July 2022. This service also performs molecular analyses to detect high-risk papillomavirus and other infections related to sexually transmitted diseases. full_description: [Åbo Akademi](https://www.abo.fi/) offers a doctoral researcher position for a maximum of 36 months within the UNCAN-Connect project, funded by the Horizon Europe Research and Innovation programme. With its strong Nordic ties, Åbo Akademi University holds an acclaimed and recognized position within research and education both nationally and internationally. Åbo Akademi University invites applications for a fixed term position as doctoral researcher in law. The appointment is full-time and located at the Department of Business and Economics and Law at [the Faculty of Human and Social Sciences](https://www.abo.fi/en/about-abo-akademi-university/faculties/faculty-of-human-and-social-sciences/) in Turku/Åbo, Finland. Background UNCAN-Connect is a five-year initiative to transform how cancer research is conducted across Europe. Funded by the Horizon Europe Research and Innovation programme, the project brings together 53 partner organizations from 19 European countries to co-develop UNCAN.eu, a decentralized collaborative platform enabling secure, ethical, and interoperable access to cancer data. UNCAN-Connect will validate its platform through use cases targeting six cancer types – pediatric, lymphoid, pancreatic, ovarian, lung, and prostate cancer – and will promote open access to cancer data while respecting patients’ rights and privacy. The School of Law at Åbo Akademi is involved with a share in the large project. Our task is to evaluate the use of AI-tools in cancer diagnostics from the viewpoint of Trustworthy AI (TAI) and develop a standard operating procedure (SOP). The EU project will focus on two parts, federated cancer data spaces and AI tools for data analysis. Our work will be on the second part, assessing the AI trustworthiness of the tools. This initially means defining a clarifying standard operating procedure for the use case partners. The position is located in Turku/Åbo, Finland. Qualifications and assessment We seek a motivated person interested in research related to the project topic, with an educational background in law or another closely related field suitable for the described position. Initiative-taking is an important asset. full_description: 5. DOCTORAL RESEARCHER IN SOLAR AND SPACE PHYSICS The Space Physics Group at the University of Helsinki invites applications for a fully funded 4-year PhD position in solar and heliophysics. The position is part of the newly funded Research Council of Finland project, Early Evolution of Magnetic Sheaths and their Space-Weather Impact on near-Sun Planets (EMSWIP), led by Dr. Ranadeep Sarkar. The preferred start date is February 2026, but later dates are negotiable. Project Background Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) are massive eruptions of magnetized plasma from the Sun that can cause severe space weather disturbances in planetary environments. These eruptions are often accompanied by turbulent sheath regions—zones of compressed plasma and magnetic fields formed between the CME-driven shock and the CME itself. While sheath regions are known to play a major role in driving geomagnetic storms on Earth, their impact on the inner planets, particularly Mercury and Venus, remains poorly understood. Sheaths are challenging to study due to their complex and multi-scale structure and their possible extended formation from the low solar corona to inter-planetary space. Most existing global MHD models are largely limited by their lower boundary at 0.1 astronomical unit and inaccuracies in CME flux-rope initialization techniques. To address these challenges, the EMSWIP project aims to develop an advanced Sun-to-planet modeling framework that captures the full evolution of CMEs and their sheath regions from the solar corona to planetary environments, validated through data from latest missions such as BepiColombo, Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter, and PUNCH. EMSWIP is expected to significantly deepen our understanding of the early evolution of CMEs and their sheath regions, as well as their space weather effects on unmagnetized or weakly magnetized planets, paving the way to uncover how similar processes shape planetary atmospheres beyond our solar system. Role of the Doctoral Researcher The selected candidate will contribute to several aspects of the project, including analyzing near-Sun observations of CMEs and shocks, running three-dimensional numerical simulations to model the Sun-to-planet evolution of CMEs and their sheath regions, assessing their impact on planetary environments, and validating the model results with in-situ measurements. Requirements MSc (or equivalent) in space physics, astrophysics, or a related discipline completed by the time of appointment; Strong interest in solar physics, space weather, or plasma modeling; Programming experience (e.g., Python or equivalent); Some background in solar data analysis or simulations is helpful, but not mandatory; Proficiency in written and spoken English. full_description: 4. Luleå University of Technology is experiencing strong growth with world-leading expertise in several research areas. We shape the future through innovative education and groundbreaking research results, and based on the Arctic region, we create global societal benefit. Our scientific and artistic research and education are conducted in close collaboration with international, national, and regional companies, public actors, and leading universities. Luleå University of Technology has a total turnover of nearly SEK 2.1 billion per year. We currently have 1,900 employees and 18,700 students. In the coming years, multi-billion investments will be made in major projects in Northern Sweden to create a fossil-free society nationally and globally. Luleå University of Technology is involved in several of these cutting-edge research projects and the societal transformations they entail. We offer a broad range of courses and study programs to match the skills in demand. We hope that you will help us build the sustainable companies and societies of the future. The Robotics and Artificial Intelligence, RAI, subject at the Department of Computer Science and Electrical and Space Engineering at Luleå University of Technology is now looking for a Researcher to contribute to our growing activities. The RAI team is conducting fundamental research in all aspects of robotics with a specific focus on aerial, space, and bioinspired robotics. Subject description Robotics and artificial intelligence aim to develop novel robotic systems characterized by advanced autonomy to improve the ability of robots to interact with the surrounding environment and humans during the execution of specific tasks. Project description The vision of RAI is aimed at closing the gap from theory to real life, while the team has strong expertise in field robotics. Specific application areas of focus are robotics for mines, aerial inspection of aging infrastructure, multi-robotic search and rescue, multi-sensor fusion, and multirobot coordination, including multirobot perception, decentralization, and mission execution. The RAI team has strong European and National participation in multiple R&D&I projects. Duties The duties of a researcher primarily comprise research. Teaching and pedagogical development work may be included, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours. You will perform research with substantial experimental components that should be published in peer-reviewed international journals and major conferences. The position includes supervision of PhD and MSc students, teaching, and support in acquiring funds for future research projects from funding agencies/councils, EU framework programs, or industry. You will work in the field of robotic autonomy and all activities will be linked with national, European, and worldwide R&D projects. Characteristic research topics will focus on, but not be limited to, the following areas, where proof of previous work with experimentally verified results is necessary: Research Topics: Field Robotics with Focus on Extreme Environments • Navigation through unknown environments • Rapid dynamics-based planning • Semantic-based Exploration • Source localization • Perception in sensor-degraded environments: • Localization in smoke and dust-filled environments • Scene awareness • Biometric/triage evaluations, etc. • Mission-specific modules such as autonomous firefighting, sampling, rescue operations, or large-scale mission planning. Qualifications To be eligible for employment as a researcher you must have a PhD or a foreign degree equivalent to a PhD in Automatic Control or related subject. A doctoral degree awarded no more than three years before the application deadline provides a useful qualification. Candidates with earlier doctoral degrees may also be considered for special reasons, e.g., statutory leaves of absence. The research tasks require a solid mathematical background with proven advanced experimental capabilities and excellent programming skills (e.g., C++, ROS, Matlab, etc.). You should have a strong vision to evaluate and demonstrate research findings in real-life operating conditions, to close the gap between pure theory and experimental verifications. You will need to represent the group in different contexts, in Sweden and abroad, hence excellent English skills are required. Further information The employment is limited to 1 year, full-time. Placement: Luleå For further information please contact: George Nikolakopoulos, Chaired Professor (+46) 920 491298, geonik@ltu.se Union representatives: SACO-S Diana Chroneer, (+46)920-49 2037 diana.chroneer@ltu.se OFR-S Marika Vesterberg, (+46)920-49 1721 marika.vesterberg@ltu.se In case of different interpretations of the English and Swedish versions of this announcement, the Swedish version takes precedence. Application We prefer you apply by clicking the apply button below. The application should include a detailed CV with full description of all scientific merits and publications, motivation letter, a research plan describing research topics, list of successful grant applications, two references, and copies of verified and translated diplomas from high school and universities. Your application must be in English. Reference number: 4683-2025 Closing date: December 1, 2025

full_description: 5. Are you a proven leader and experienced manager with data science expertise? We are looking for a new Head of Data Science to join our Research department and lead our talented data scientists and engineers striving to enable safer use of medicines and vaccines for everyone everywhere. Interviews will be held on an ongoing basis. Since 1978, Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) has been dedicated to developing, supporting, and expanding the field of pharmacovigilance science and practice. As a World Health Organization (WHO) Collaborating Centre, we support work around the world to examine the potential adverse effects of medicines and vaccines and contribute to safer, more informed care of patients. We are a diverse, international group of pharmacists, physicians, data scientists, system developers, communicators, and many other professionals motivated by a deep belief that the work we do matters. About the role We are seeking a Head of Data Science to join our Research Department. You will report to our Head of Research. The Research department's areas of focus and expertise include data-driven discovery for observational medical data, and computational methods to support and enhance human decision-making throughout pharmacovigilance. We work with advanced methods in natural language processing, statistical pattern discovery and machine learning, collaborate internationally, and share our results in Open Access scientific publications. To get the best possible results, we have adopted an agile approach to scientific development, where scientists collaborate closely across disciplines in agile teams, with a common focus and joint responsibilities. We believe that mastery, purpose, and autonomy for individuals and teams are key enablers to achieve scientific excellence. What you will do - Manage a group of around 10 data scientists and engineers. - Provide strategic leadership for the data science and engineering function - define and prioritise key processes for model development, deployment, and lifecycle management; ensure effective cross-departmental collaboration with colleagues responsible for digital infrastructure and user-facing applications; and foster ways of working that integrate scientific rigour with practical impact. - Ensure the right expertise within the Data Science section through strategic competence development and recruitment. - Work in close partnership with the Head of Pharmacovigilance Science, the Agile Coach, and staff to lead the operations of UMC’s Research department and create the conditions for agile teams to succeed. You will ensure strategic alignment, foster collaboration, and uphold scientific rigour while empowering teams to decide how best to achieve their goals. - Stay abreast of technological developments within data science and engineering. Your qualifications - A Master’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field. You have - Proven leadership abilities, with at least three years’ experience managing teams of data scientists, engineers, or researchers. - Strong foundation in data analysis and machine learning, with the ability to engage confidently in technical discussions and coach staff (our teams primarily work with Python, R, and SQL), complemented by broad knowledge across the data science field. - Experience working across organizational boundaries and engaging effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders. - An ability to communicate effectively in English, which is our working language. It is an advantage, if you have - Worked with cloud platforms, DevOps and MLOps. - Worked within agile settings and processes. - Experience of scientific development, evaluation, and dissemination. - Experience from the biomedical or pharmaceutical sector. - Experience working with a variety of data sources. - A PhD or licentiate degree. Personal profile At UMC we believe that scientific excellence flourishes when empowered teams are trusted, supported, and inspired. As Head of Data Science, you share that philosophy - creating clarity and context rather than control, and enabling scientists to take ownership, collaborate openly, and dare to be bold in their ideas and their science. You cultivate an environment where people feel safe to challenge and be challenged, and where mastery, autonomy, and purpose guide how work gets done. You are a confident leader and a warm colleague who builds trust and connection across disciplines. You combine strategic vision with the ability to prioritise and deliver results, even amid competing demands. You lead yourself as well as others - showing integrity, resilience, and balance - and you set an example through open communication, active listening, and respect for diverse perspectives. Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) is an independent, self-funded, non-profit foundation established in 1978 dedicated to safer use of medicines and vaccines. Through an agreement between the Government of Sweden and the World Health Organization (WHO), UMC operates the Programme for International Drug Monitoring, supporting over 180 member countries and regions in strengthening safety surveillance, and maintains VigiBase, the WHO global database of adverse event reports. In addition, UMC provides international standards and related digital solutions for secure exchange of pharmacovigilance data, including a global medicine and vaccine terminology for identification of medicinal products. With around 200 staff, UMC advances the science of pharmacovigilance and transforms its practice through technological innovation. UMC’s working language is English. You will find the contact details at the end of this page. UMC follows the collective agreements between the Swedish Agency for Government Employers and Saco-S and ST. full_description: 4. Help shape the future of vision–language models for medical imaging to solve real clinical challenges! This doctoral student position offers the chance to explore cutting-edge multimodal AI - integrating PET/CT images, radiology reports, and clinical data - to develop more accurate and trustworthy diagnostic tools. You will join a dynamic, interdisciplinary research group with extensive international collaborations and access to large, high-quality clinical datasets. About us The Computer Vision Group at the Department of Electrical Engineering conducts research in the field of automatic image interpretation and perceptual scene understanding. The group targets both medical applications, such as the development of new and more effective methods and systems for analysis, support, and diagnostics, as well as general computer vision applications including autonomously guided vehicles (particularly self-driving cars), image-based localization, structure-from-motion, and object recognition. The main research problems include mathematical theory, algorithms, and machine learning (deep learning) for inverse problems in artificial intelligence, as well as application to medical problems. About the research project This doctoral student position is part of a new research project focused on developing next-generation AI methods for medical image analysis. The overall goal is to build vision–language models (VLMs) that learn jointly from medical images and the corresponding radiology reports, with the aim of improving diagnostic accuracy, disease localization, and model explainability. The research will explore how combining multimodal data - such as PET/CT scans, radiology text reports, and clinical information - can help AI systems better understand complex medical image patterns. A key idea is to use text as privileged information during training, enabling models that can provide reliable, image-only predictions at scan time. The project also includes developing weakly supervised methods for disease localization without requiring pixel-level annotations. The work spans several core areas: machine learning, computer vision, deep learning, and medical imaging. The successful candidate will design and implement new AI models, carry out large-scale experiments on clinical datasets, and collaborate closely with medical researchers and clinicians. Our research group is highly interdisciplinary and works with national and international partners in both academia and healthcare. Who we are looking for Mandatory qualifications: • Master’s degree of 120 credits or a Master’s degree of 60 credits* in a relevant field such as physics, mathematics or computer science. The PhD project also forms part of a broader research initiative (Sustainable Supply of CRMs) that aims to integrate ore geology, political science, and law to jointly explore whether, and how, CRMs can be extracted and recycled in a sustainable and just way. Subject description Ore Geology includes the use, setting and mode of formation of naturally occurring economic concentrations of metallic raw materials. The research aims at describing the geological conditions that lead to economic concentrations of minerals, as well as how these minerals can be used for a sustainable societal development. Project description Northern Sweden hosts several metamorphic graphite occurrences within Paleoproterozoic metasupracrustal successions. This project will investigate the geological evolution and mineralogical quality of the Nunasvaara graphite deposit in northern Norrbotten – one of Europe’s most significant natural graphite resources and an EU-designated strategic CRM project. The work will combine field mapping, structural geology and geochronology with petrography, bulk rock and mineral characterization (lithogeochemistry, XRD), and detailed microanalysis (e.g., SEM-WDS, electron microprobe, Raman spectroscopy, SIMS). The PhD student will integrate these methods to better understand how sedimentary processes, deformation and metamorphism combine to control natural graphite mineralization, crystallinity and quality. Results will generate new information about the tectonic and metamorphic evolution of Paleoproterozoic greenstone belts in northern Fennoscandia and the genesis of metamorphic graphite deposits. Duties A doctoral student position involves both theoretical and practical work. The doctoral student is trained in scientific work in the form of publishing scientific articles in journals and presenting at national and international conferences. A doctoral student also takes compulsory and optional doctoral courses. In addition, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to teach or perform other educational tasks. As a PhD researcher, you work independently in many contexts, which provides an opportunity to learn how to manage and run a challenging project. Most of your working hours will be devoted to your own doctoral studies. Project work will mainly include geological field mapping, outcrop sampling, sample preparation, geochemical analysis, microanalytical characterization of geological samples, and writing scientific papers. For this project, a willingness and ability to work outdoors in rural areas with uneven terrain and occasional inclement weather is important. Qualifications We seek a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in structural and metamorphic geology and enthusiasm for integrating analytical and field approaches. Eligible applicants for the position must have excellent academic grades and recently obtained their master's degree or equivalent degree in Earth Sciences with specialization in mineralogy, petrology, ore geology, or other relevant subjects. Geological mapping with a focus on structures is an important part of the PhD project and experience in this is a merit. Experience of analytical techniques (e.g., XRD, Raman) is also considered a strong merit. It is important that the applicant can express themselves well in English, both orally and in writing. Thus, written proof of good English language skills (certificate of examination, relevant transcripts of records, or a letter of support) is required. Postdoc position in neutron scattering and vibrational spectroscopy studies of perovskite materials for energy applications Do you want to perform cutting-edge, needs-driven basic research on halide perovskites for next-generation energy technologies, using and developing advanced methodologies and neutron techniques? Do you also want to work in an international and highly dynamic research environment? Then apply for this postdoctoral position! About the research project Halide perovskites (HPs) are an emerging class of highly interesting photoluminescent materials, with possible utilization in advanced optoelectronic devices, such as energy efficient solar panels and light emitting diodes (LEDs). A critical challenge in this field pertains to understanding the nature and role of atomic-scale (local) structure and dynamics, which underlie the photophysical properties of these materials. Experimentally, these structural and dynamical properties can be vigorously investigated with neutron spectroscopy (INS and QENS), but a formidable task is to study the behavior of the materials under conditions that mimic those in operating devices, such as under photoexcitation. This postdoc project focuses on the use and development of experimental methodologies and neutron techniques for the study of local structure and dynamics in HPs, especially under operationally relevant conditions, with a view towards their usage in technological applications. The postdoc will be part of a new collaborative project between researchers at Chalmers University of Technology and the European Spallation Source (ESS) in Sweden, and ISIS Neutron and Muon Source in the U.K. About us The postdoc will be based in the Division of Energy and Materials at the Department of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Chalmers University of Technology, Sweden. Here, the Karlsson group focuses on characterization of structure and dynamics in “functional” materials, with a view towards their implementation in energy-relevant technologies, such as LEDs, solar cells, batteries and fuel cells, and for catalysis. The research is mainly experimental in nature, and the group is highly experienced in the use and development of techniques at large-scale neutron and photon sources, vibrational spectroscopy, and optical techniques. Typically, the work is carried out in close collaboration with other leading research groups, in Sweden and in several other countries, which provide complementary expertise in materials synthesis and/or computer simulations. Qualifications We are looking for a highly motivated person with a background in neutron spectroscopy on solid-state materials. Expertise in vibrational spectroscopy (Raman and infrared), especially from time-resolved experiments, or in measurements of photoluminescence, is an asset. Applicants must hold (or be relatively soon to finish) a PhD in Physics, Materials Science, or a related discipline. The PhD degree should be awarded no more than three years prior to the application deadline. About us The Division of Electric Power Engineering conducts research across a broad spectrum of electric power technologies. Our mission is to foster interdisciplinary research within the university and with external partners. Our work is organized into four main areas: Electric power systems, power electronics, electric machines, and high-voltage engineering. The strength of our research lies in its solid theoretical foundation, complemented by extensive experimental verification in both laboratory and field environments. We aim to advance the understanding of electrical power systems for renewable energy, vehicles, buildings, and industrial applications. The division has been actively involved in research projects funded by the EU, Swedish state agencies, and the Swedish power industry, covering topics such as active distribution grids, microgrids, smart buildings, etc. About the research project This postdoctoral position focuses on developing and demonstrating solutions that enable the concept of “Energy Islanding as a Service”. This concept will showcase capabilities of an energy island to not only optimally supply its own energy demands and support the grids in normal conditions but also to securely and optimally supply its critical services in critical situations and to support the grids with the black-start power for grid restoration. The position will, in collaboration with other researchers in the project, focus on developing: • A measurement and control platform for optimal island operation of Chalmers’ wind-battery system. • Machine learning-based forecasting tools for renewable production using limited local measurement data. • An adaptable multi-timescale energy management system for energy islands. • Models for ancillary service provision to transmission and distribution system operators (TSOs and DSOs). • Real-time operation and control solutions using grid-forming (GFM) controllers for both grid-connected and islanded operation. The Chalmers wind turbine with battery storage (link) will serve as the validation platform for the developed models and systems. The PhD degree must have been awarded no more than three years prior to the application deadline*. The ideal candidate has: • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, • A solid academic record, and • Excellent command of English, both spoken and written. It is desirable that applicants have expertise in one or more of the following: • Energy management and control for energy islands, • Electricity and ancillary service markets, • Programming (e.g., Python, GAMS) and power system simulation tools, • Development of measurement and IoT-based data exchange systems.
